message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties that make it unique among the elements. Below is a concise overview of its key characteristics:

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (²H, 0.02 %), Tritium (³H, trace) |
| **Physical Properties (at 25 °C, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (≈1/14 of air) |
| | Boiling point | –252.8 °C (20.27 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ (STP) |
| | Diffusivity | Extremely high (≈0.1 cm² s⁻¹ in air) |
| **Thermodynamic Data** | Standard enthalpy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.000 kJ mol⁻¹ (since it’s a gas at STP) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂O₂, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive as a radical (H•) and as a nucleophile (H⁻) in hydrides; forms covalent bonds with many elements; reacts with halogens, metals, and non‑metals under appropriate conditions. |
| | Combustion | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺). |
| | Isotopic chemistry | Deuterium and tritium form heavier analogues of all hydrogen compounds; used in nuclear fusion (DT reaction). |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N (protium), 0 (deuterium), 2.978 µ_N (tritium) |
| | Stability | Protium and deuterium stable; tritium β‑decays (half‑life ≈ 12.32 y). |
| **Applications & Significance** | Energy carrier | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant (LH₂/LOX). |
| | Industrial uses | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions, semiconductor manufacturing. |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (water only); storage and transport challenges (low density, high diffusivity). |
| | Scientific importance | Benchmark element for quantum chemistry; used in spectroscopy, isotope labeling, and as a probe in astrophysics (H I 21‑cm line). |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the cosmos.
- **Diatomic gas**: Exists as H₂ under normal conditions; each molecule contains two protons and two electrons.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide variety of compounds, from simple hydrides to complex organic molecules.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (¹H) is the most common, but deuterium (²H) and tritium (³H) play crucial roles in nuclear science and isotope labeling.
- **Energy relevance**: Hydrogen is central to emerging clean‑energy technologies (fuel cells, hydrogen‑powered vehicles, fusion research).

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
